title: The presumption against implied repeal
summary: The presumption generally favors reading a new statute consistently with an existing one unless the statutes are irreconcilable or the new enactment is intended to supersede the earlier scheme.
notes: Katzmann names this principle as an example of a longstanding canon. The question is whether two enacted provisions can continue to operate together and, if not, how the newer legislation changes the older rule. This source gives a definition and examples of competing interpretive tools, not the separately assigned harmonization cases. Epic Systems and Trump v. Illinois are on file (added-sources) and briefed in their own entries.
